overview: This 132-page file traces Japan’s move toward state control of electric power from 1932 to 1938. U.S. Embassy reports and memoranda document political opposition, legislation, and concerns for private companies and foreign bondholders. Translated laws, ordinances, membership lists, and facility schedules show how the new Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company was established and supplied with assets. A separate telegram concerns a threatened substation at Tsingtao.
keywords: Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company
interest: Translated laws and transfer schedules let historians trace how state control affected private assets and foreign creditors.
